section.p: Areas of Shallow Flooding: A designated AO or AH zone on a community's FIRM with a one 22 percent or greater annual chance of flooding to an average depth of one to three feet where a 23 clearly defined channel does not exist, where the path of flooding is unpredictable, and where 24 velocity flow may be evident. Such flooding is characterized by ponding or sheet flow. 25 Base Flood: The flood having a one percent (1%) chance of being equaled or exceeded in any 27 given year. 28 Base Flood Elevation (BFE): The elevation of the water surface elevation resulting from a flood 30 that has a one percent (1%) chance of equaling or exceeding that level in any given year. On 31 the Flood Insurance Rate Map the elevation is usually in feet, in relation to the National 32 Geodetic Vertical Datum of 1929, the North American Vertical Datum of 1988, or other datum 33 referenced in the Flood Insurance Study report, or the average depth of the base flood, usually 34 in feet, above the ground surface. Base flood elevations are shown at selected intervals on 35 maps of Special Flood Hazard Areas that are determined by detailed methods.
